questions.q: How does the app container reach the database container in a Compose project?
o: By the service name, such as db:5432
By localhost, since both run on one host
By the host IP and a random port number
By the container ID printed after startup
questions.w: Compose creates a project network with DNS by service name. Inside a container, localhost means that container itself.

questions.q: What does depends_on do by default?
o: Controls start order only, waiting for the container to start
Waits until the database accepts connections before starting the app
Restarts the app whenever the dependency restarts
Copies the dependency's environment into the app
questions.w: Default is service_started. For readiness use a healthcheck and depends_on with condition: service_healthy, and still retry connections in the app.

questions.q: Which command removes containers, the network and also the named volumes (deleting database data)?
o: docker compose down -v
docker compose stop
docker compose down
docker compose rm --force
questions.w: down keeps named volumes; the -v flag deletes them too. Use it for a deliberately clean start.

questions.q: How do you keep database data between container restarts?
o: Mount a named volume at the database data directory
Publish the database port to the host
Set restart: always on the database service
Put the data in an environment variable
questions.w: Named volumes are managed by Docker and survive container removal. Restart policy and port publishing do not store data.

o: Settings merged automatically over compose.yaml, usually for local development
A replacement file that disables compose.yaml completely
A list of secrets that Compose encrypts at rest
A cache of images built on the previous run
questions.w: Compose merges compose.override.yaml over the base file by default. Use -f to layer other files, such as a production file.

questions.q: Why prefer Testcontainers for automated integration tests rather than a shared Compose environment?
o: Containers are created per test run with random ports and removed afterwards
Testcontainers is the only tool that can start PostgreSQL
Compose cannot run in a continuous integration job
Compose files cannot contain a database service
questions.w: Isolation and repeatability: each run starts clean. Compose suits the developer's long-running local environment.

o: A label that makes a service optional, started with --profile
A saved set of CPU and memory limits for all services
A user account used to pull private images
A template that generates a Dockerfile
questions.w: Services with profiles start only when the profile is enabled (--profile debug or COMPOSE_PROFILES); services without one always start.

questions.q: Why is Docker Compose not used to run production clusters?
o: It manages one host: no scheduling across machines or rolling updates
It cannot start more than three containers at a time on any host
It forbids the use of volumes and networks in a project
It only works with Windows containers and a licensed Docker Desktop
questions.w: Compose is excellent for local development and small single-host setups. Kubernetes provides orchestration across nodes.
